title: Field
summary: A field is a commutative arithmetic system where every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared abstract algebra context is fixed.

content.plain: A field is a commutative arithmetic system where every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.
content.exact: A field (F,+,·) is a commutative ring with 1≠0 such that F\{0} is an abelian group under multiplication.
content.example: ℚ and ℝ are fields; ℤ is not.
content.caveat: Finite and infinite fields can behave very differently.
